.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r15/task/solution/solve.sh, solution/app/package.json, grep of solution/app/src/runtime.ts and server.js for the isolation mechanism

qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r15/raw-evidence-index.json (all 22 artifact hashes recomputed and matching) and qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/results/{editor,runtime,polish,persist-before,persist-after,restart}.json
evidence:
REACHABILITY. instruction.md:3 says 'the six notes in /instructions'; exactly six notes ship (behaviour, integration, overview, policy, security, ui) and environment/Dockerfile:14-15 copies them and /assets. Every runtime claim in integration.md is true of the launcher: integration.md:3 'node /app/server.js from a working directory that may be outside /app ... PORT is set to 3000' and integration.md:9 'If DB_PATH is set, open that absolute path instead, including when the app runs from a writable copy outside /app' match tests/test.sh:97-111 (env -i with PATH, NODE_PATH, PORT=3000, DB_PATH, uid 65534, optional /tmp/submission copy); the symlink rule at integration.md:11 matches test.sh:72-83. Express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1 are pinned identically in environment/Dockerfile:9-12 and tests/Dockerfile, both on Node 22, with network_mode public in both phases (task.toml:22,38), so parser/formatter libraries and a browser for self-testing are obtainable; fonts-noto-color-emoji is in the verifier image for the emoji requirement. The hard capabilities are all reachable with web-platform means and are demonstrated by the golden: sandboxed srcdoc iframe plus a meta CSP (solution/app/src/runtime.ts:363-389) gives preview isolation, fetch rejection, refusal of eval/Function/WebAssembly/Worker/dynamic import, and inline handler attributes; loop budget, Stop, last-good restore with input values and canvas, whole-file HTML error lines and Promise-rejection lines are implemented there too. Scripted golden on these bytes (hashes verified): all 52 scripted entries true with pageErrors [] across results/editor.json, runtime.json, polish.json, persist-before.json, persist-after.json, and restart.json shows the same record and history [2,1] after a real process restart. That is scripted evidence of achievability, not a configured judge run; no judge run exists for these bytes, and I claim no Oracle or model score from it.

AMBIGUITY. I looked for a second reasonable reading of each requirement and compared it with the graded steps; none leads a conforming build to a different product than the one graded. Places where the notes leave a choice are either stated as a choice or graded tolerantly: undo granularity for single-caret typing (ui.md:9 'in one step or character by character'; cw_undo_restores_caret says 'Press Undo repeatedly'), triple-click line break ('with or without its line break'), indent width for Tab ('gains the same indent'), about five seconds for the live library (criteria allow ten), refused-or-appended for an old-revision restore (behaviour.md:13 'must not overwrite a newer save'; cw_history_restore_retry accepts both), refuse-whole-draft or refuse-the-call for dynamic evaluation (cw_dynamic_code_refused accepts both), static or live restored picture (behaviour.md:5 'A restored picture may be static'). The repeat-safe restore is stated publicly and concretely (behaviour.md:13 'Send saves and restores as ordinary HTTP requests ... If the same restore request is sent again after it was already committed ... it must not create another revision'), and the five-second budget is defined for source, pending callbacks and later interactions (behaviour.md:5).

NOTES (ungraded or tolerated ambiguities, reported as the row requires; none is a defect on these bytes): (1) behaviour.md:3 asks for 'a one-based line number for ... a Promise rejection that nothing handles' and says 'the message is the text of the Error or rejected value'; for a rejection with a non-Error value the browser gives no line, so that edge is not strictly reachable. The graded cases (cw_promise_rejection_message_and_line) reject only with new Error, where the stack supplies the line. (2) security.md:3 says the preview 'must not be able to reach the network' and then names only fetch; whether img/script/link subresources in a user HTML file must also be blocked is open. Only fetch is graded. (3) behaviour.md:5 restores the last-good picture when a run 'throws, is stopped or exceeds the five-second run budget'; a syntax-error run, a refused dynamic-evaluation run, an unhandled rejection, and the case with no earlier successful run are not addressed. None is graded for restore. (4) Under behaviour.md:5 a legitimate endless animation (setInterval that never stops) is ended at five seconds as a time-limit failure; this is the single reading and the criteria agree, but it is a surprising product rule that a builder may second-guess. (5) ui.md:17 returns focus to the code 'after ... a replacement' while ui.md:11 selects the following match after Replace current, so the next keystroke would overwrite that match; consistent but awkward, and only Replace all is graded for focus. (6) ui.md:5 'Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End (Cmd on a Mac)' is not the usual Mac binding; irrelevant in the Linux Chromium verifier. (7) ui.md:3 allows 'a small input' for plumbing while cw_custom_document_surface allows 'a small input or textarea'; the criterion is the more lenient one, so no conforming build is harmed. (8) The Internal Quality Checks sheet words this row 'with no network'; the public sheet and the skill delivery profile say network is public, and I applied the public wording.
